images_added_23_sept_2026_transcription_.shows: Folio 20 recto (period ink foliation confirmed, docket 'C. Carpi 1526'): Alberto Pio de Carpi to Madame [Louise de Savoie]. About 20 lines plain French, then 9 lines of cipher (rows 3-11) ending abruptly at the foot of the page with no closing -- the letter continues onto the verso (see f24 below). Transcribed in ciphertext.txt (single pass, see reconciliation.md).

ONE photographed opening = folio 20 VERSO (left page: 22 lines cipher, then 2 plain paragraphs) + folio 21 RECTO (right page, period foliation '21' visible top right: 13 more cipher lines, then 2 plain closing paragraphs, date 'Rome ce xxvij [27] jour d'Octobre l'an mil Vc xxv [1525]', signed 'de Carpi'). This is the letter's actual ending; item 20 therefore spans 3 page-sides, not 1 (see ciphertext.txt header for the full correction and the date discrepancy against the finding aid's '22 oct.'). NOT transcribed past folio 20 recto this session; crops saved in crops/ for a follow-up pass.

Next opening after f24: folio 21 VERSO (left page, address panel with a wax-seal hole and mirror show-through of the letter's own last lines -- the outer wrapper of the folded letter, blank apart from the address) + a blank facing page. Confirms the letter's true close is on folio 21 recto (f24-right), not here; no further cipher.

note: Canvas-to-folio offset in this volume grows through the early gathering (canvas16=folio16, offset0; canvas21=folio19, offset+2; canvas23=folio20, offset+3; f34=folio28, offset+6) and is NOT linear -- extra unfoliated address/wrapper leaves are inserted irregularly (confirmed: f25 is folio 21's own wrapper, a leaf with no foliation of its own). Do not extrapolate folio position from a fixed per-canvas offset; read the period ink foliation (small numeral, top right of most rectos) directly from a full-resolution fetch instead. Folio 28 (Raince to Madame, item 28) is now located and characterised (f34-f36, see above) -- the 20 Sept sweep's 'not located' note for it is superseded. The four 1535 'Dechiffrement' leaves (ff.56, 60, 72, 76) were NOT located in this pass: canvases sampled at reduced width without success were f58, f60, f62, f64, f66, f68, f70, f72, f74, f76, f78 (a period annotation resembling 'Segrement'/cipher-related marginalia was seen near f64 but not confirmed as one of the four items); a denser bracket or the reading-room folio-search box would be needed next.

image_prep_pass_23_sept_2026.brief: fetch full-resolution IIIF images for every canvas carrying folio 28 (Raince to Madame: f34, f35, f36) and folio 24 (Raince to Robertet: f29, f30, f31), then cut line-level crops for transcription.
image_prep_pass_23_sept_2026.requests: gallica.bnf.fr: 6 info.json + 6 successful full-resolution image fetches on the first pass, then 5 more full-resolution refetches (f29, f30, f34, f35, f36) after a line-detection parameter fix required re-cropping from source (f29's first refetch attempt hit 2 connection resets on the full-width request and was fetched once at reduced width [/full/6500,/] as a fallback, then the full-width fetch succeeded on a later retry and superseded it; every other fetch succeeded on its first attempt) = 17 image fetches total, all through the same good-citizen 1.5s-apart, descriptive-UA pattern as prior sweeps.
image_prep_pass_23_sept_2026.line_detection_method: images/crop.py takes a row ink-density profile per page-column and finds line centres as local maxima (scipy find_peaks, distance=85px, prominence=40). An initial calibration at distance=110 (chosen to match an eyeballed ~22-line count for folio 24 recto from a 900px thumbnail) turned out to silently skip every other line in the tightly-spaced cipher blocks (true pitch there is ~95-105px, not the ~200px of the surrounding plain prose) -- caught by viewing a debug overlay of detected line-centres on the source image before finalising crops, not by eye alone. distance=85 was verified by the same method (overlay + zoom, both on a plain-prose region and a cipher region) to hit exactly one line per row of writing throughout, with no double-detection and no skipped lines. True per-page line counts are therefore roughly double the ~22/17/28/28/27/27 estimated in the 23 Sept transcription-pass NOTES.md paragraph: 42 (folio 24r), 27 (folio 24v), 41 (folio 28r), 39 (folio 28v), 39 (folio 29r), 38 (folio 29v) = 226 lines, cropped as 115 two-line bands x 2 horizontal segments (each page-column is 3200-3900px wide, over the 2400px cap) = 230 crop files in crops/, quality 60 (lowered from the planned 80/70 to keep the folder under 30MB -- see below). This does not change any of the earlier extent/token-count prose in NOTES.md or ciphertext_f28.txt, which described paragraph/line counts by eye, not a pitch-calibrated count; a future transcriber should use these corrected counts, not the earlier ones.
image_prep_pass_23_sept_2026.folder_size: The full IIIF fetches (8299-8315 x 6214px, ~3.3-5.9MB each) are cropped from directly, then REPLACED in img/ with 1600px-wide, quality-80 reference copies (matching the convention already used for f25 and the prior f34/f35/f36 placeholders) -- keeping the full 8300px source in the repo made the target folder exceed 30MB even after dropping the prior placeholders, so the tradeoff taken is: crops keep full native-pixel detail (cut before any downsizing), img/ keeps only a orientation-scale reference, and this manifest records each canvas's IIIF URL and native dimensions so a full-resolution copy can be refetched on demand. Folder size after this pass: 29.2MB (checked by du -sb), under the 30MB cap.
